column1: # Family 6 battery — the zero-width-iteration span protocol of quantified
# captures, as replayable expected-value data (JUR-compat WBS item 4a).
# Columns: id <TAB> sub <TAB> pattern <TAB> input <TAB> JUR <TAB> RE2
#   sub: A = sub-family A (greedy min-0 directly on a capture whose body is
#        all-zero-width — java's GroupCurly rollback), B = sub-family B
#        (greedy quantifier on an empty-capable non-deterministic body —
#        java's Prolog+Loop surfaces the final zero-width iteration).
#        Agree-shaped rows (same answer in both protocols) carry the
#        sub-family of the fix that owns them.
#   input: "\s" escapes a space (trailing spaces stay visible), "\n" a newline.
#   JUR / RE2 protocol: M=<whole spans>|F=<first find from 0>|R=<find from
#   JUR column recorded from a live JDK (26) and re-verified against the
#        live java.util.regex oracle on every test run (the spec source).
#   RE2 column recorded from the engine's shipped default lane (VM and ASM
#        tiers agreed bit-for-bit at record time) and asserted on both
#        tiers — the RE2-lane-unchanged contract items 4b/4c must keep.
#   The JUR-lane engine assertions live in Family6BatteryTest: sub-family
#        A is LIVE (WBS 4b — the parse mark + SET_NIL finals override);
#        sub-family B stays dark until WBS 4c.
